rendered: The anode-free full cell uses a pyrite cathode, FeS2 (iron pyrite).[1] Because pyrite natively contains no sodium, the cathode is presodiated before cell assembly: the pyrite cathode is presodiated prior to cell assembly, and the full cell is built with that presodiated pyrite paired with carbon/Al current collectors in a discharged state. Sodium is then removed from the pyrite on the first charge and reduced onto the carbon/Al collector to form sodium metal in situ, so the cell contains no sodium metal on assembly.[2][3] The cathode capacity assumed for the energy density is an FeS2 capacity of 335 mAh/g[4], with the energy density calculated on the mass of the presodiated pyrite assuming a Na1.5FeS2 stoichiometry and the carbon nucleation layer.[5]
